title: The crash and talking pictures hit working musicians
summary: Wilson and Hinton recall the 1929 crash, The Jazz Singer and theatre bandsmen losing jobs, and later meeting again in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: So that was about in 19 -- well, we're almost in the thirties now, right?
And of course, as far as making a living in music, the stock market crashed right about that time, and we were just in time to hear the musicians talking about how good times had been.
Aha, me and you, we had the same finish.
Along with that stock market crash and the beginning of the Great Depression, the sound movie was invented, you know?
And The Cold Diggers of Broadway, all that stuff, utilizing music on the screen.
And you stopped all the bands in the theatres.
Right, so we were hit doubly hard -- the overall economy and then our own profession, with the theatre musicians being thrown out of work. But we managed somehow, I guess.

Well, it was a tough survival. You and I were there, and we saw it -- because I remember, I was in Chicago, and I remember when Everett Barksdale came over to Chicago, and you eventually came to Chicago, too.
Yeah, because I was instrumental in getting Everett the gig with Eddie South, and you played -- where did you play? Club DeLisa, and ...
I played with Eddie Mallory. Yeah.
